2026-08-07T04:03:50.0198048Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0199271Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0199672Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0200567Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0201020Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0201533Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0205447Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0207231Z >
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0210213Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0212813Z >
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0213627Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0214399Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0214572Z ### How to Use
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0215156Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0216219Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0216966Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0217146Z ```bash
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0217730Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0218458Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0219068Z ```
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0219275Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0219539Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0220065Z ```bash
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0221017Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0221846Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0223483Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0224927Z ```
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0225233Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0225935Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0226815Z ```bash
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0227386Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0228079Z ```
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0228279Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0228812Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0229399Z ```bash
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0229926Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0233119Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0233884Z ```
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0235147Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0236183Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0238335Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0239789Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0244048Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0244245Z ```bash
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0244707Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0245991Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0246851Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0247162Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0247712Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0249755Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0250586Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0251053Z ```
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0251720Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0252801Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0253755Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0253923Z ```bash
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0254666Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0255572Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0257258Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0257722Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0258672Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0261410Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0262027Z ```
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0262958Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0263188Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0264080Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0265063Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0266998Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0268125Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0269342Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0269892Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0270060Z ### Notes
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0270288Z 
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0270904Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0272295Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0273742Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0274987Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0276178Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0277332Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0278304Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0278990Z </mcp-clis>
2026-08-07T04:03:50.0279385Z <github-context>
